newsitem.title: UK: Reformist leads in Russian election - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Reformist leads in Russian election - Interfax.

text.p: Reformist candidate Ivan Sklyarov led his Communist rival on Monday in preliminary results of a governorship election seen as an unofficial referendum on Russia's reforms, Interfax news agency said.
Interfax, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said that with about half the ballot counted, Sklyarov had 52.52 percent of the vote against 42.26 percent for Communist Gennady Khodyrev.

The two were contesting a run-off vote on Sunday for the governorship of Nizhny Novgorod, a city of 1.5 million people on the Volga River which under the previous incumbent, Boris Nemtsov, was a pioneer of radical free-market reform.
Nemtsov, a rising star in Russian politics, was summoned to Moscow by President Boris Yeltsin in March to take the post of first deputy prime minister with a brief to accelerate reform nationwide.
Interfax said the preliminary count came from the Regional Electoral Commission. Full results were expected later on Monday.
